comparison: Perfect agreement on behavioral serial dependence findings (C39-C45). Both evaluations find the behavioral evidence robust and well-supported, with appropriate statistical methods. OpenEval emphasizes methodological soundness while peer reviewers note replication of prior findings without criticism.

Agreement on successful reconstruction findings (C48-C52). Both evaluations accept the IEM methodology and reconstruction results as valid. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers also accept findings while noting some concerns about interpretation of what drives reconstructions.

Significant disagreement on interpretation of key findings (C53-C57). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with clear timing pattern evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns that the pattern could reflect differential noise susceptibility rather than post-perceptual timing, and noting lack of feature-specificity analysis and temporal averaging limitations.

Agreement on brain-behavior correlation findings (C58-C60, C79-C80). Both evaluations accept the temporal specificity of correlations during retro-cue phase. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers implicitly accept findings while requesting additional temporal precision analysis.

Agreement on reactivation findings (C61-C64, C70). Both evaluations accept the replication of prior work and identification of second reactivation period. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED without challenges to the data or analysis.

Disagreement on eye movement confound control (C65-C67). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, stating the control analysis demonstrates eye movements did not drive MEG findings. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 raising substantial concerns that the analysis only considers gaze angle not amplitude, and requesting additional analyses to directly decode from gaze coordinates and test for history-dependent gaze patterns.

Agreement on S1 reconstruction during S2 epoch findings (C85-C86, C88). Both evaluations accept the empirical observation without challenge. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while acknowledging 'hidden state' interpretation involves inference from literature; peer reviewers similarly accept findings without contesting the interpretation.

Partial disagreement on sample size adequacy (C37-C38, C101, C103). OpenEval rates methodological details as SUPPORTED, noting power analysis justification though acknowledging conservative approach. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 expressing concern that n=10 is 'at the lower end' and recommending larger samples for future studies, though accepting it as marginal given within-subject design.

Partial overlap on timing interpretation (C71, C76, C91-C92 vs C11-C12, C76, C78, C91, C98). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing methodological advantages and post-encoding account support. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 proposing alternative interpretation that results could reflect increasing noise over time rather than post-perceptual timing, and requesting finer temporal analysis.

Partial overlap on main conclusions (C68, C77-C78, C97-C98 vs C53-C57, C68, C77). OpenEval rates synthesis claims as SUPPORTED, justifying 'first direct neural signature' claim. Peer evaluation of overlapping claims (C68, C77) is embedded in UNCERTAIN rating for broader finding, with concerns about alternative interpretations and temporal averaging.

Partial overlap on timing conclusions (C68, C77-C78, C97-C98 vs C11-C12, C76, C78, C91, C98). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with well-justified timing interpretation. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN rating reflects fundamental concerns about whether timing pattern reflects post-perceptual processes or differential noise susceptibility across epochs.
